text: Step 5 of the investigation plan: applying the fix Lesson 6 diagnosed. The missing-index report gave you exactly what's needed — PatientID as the key, and InvoiceDate, Amount, Status, and ProviderID as included columns. CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX builds that covering index directly from the report, nothing invented.

Now re-run the exact same query Lesson 5 captured a plan for, with Ctrl+M still on. Don't change the query itself — changing both the index and the query at once would make it impossible to tell which change actually fixed anything. One variable at a time.

The new plan tells the real story. The Clustered Index Scan from Lesson 5 is gone, replaced by an Index Seek on the new index — straight to the rows for this one PatientID. The Sort operator is gone too, because the index already stores rows in an order that supports it.

It feels faster isn't evidence — table size, server load, and caching can all make a query feel different for reasons that have nothing to do with the fix. A new captured execution plan showing Index Seek instead of Clustered Index Scan is a structural change, and that's real proof.

This closes Billing's complaint, with concrete before-and-after proof. But Scheduling's appointment-calendar complaint from Lesson 1 is still completely unexplained — nothing in this fix touches dbo dot Appointments. Lesson 8 picks that up as a separate, second root cause.
